articles.title: Tactical Defense Fundamentals: Building Your Foundation
articles.excerpt: Whether you're a first-time shooter or an experienced professional, mastering the fundamentals is the non-negotiable foundation of tactical proficiency.
articles.body:
## Why Fundamentals Matter

In tactical training, there are no shortcuts. Every advanced skill—from room-clearing to vehicle extraction—is built on a foundation of mastered fundamentals.

## The Four Pillars

**1. Stance and Platform** — Your platform is your base of stability under recoil and stress.

**2. Grip** — A proper high-grip, thumbs-forward grip reduces muzzle flip.

**3. Sight Alignment and Picture** — The front sight is your truth.

**4. Trigger Control** — Trigger reset is the secret most shooters don't learn until years in. We teach it on Day 1.
articles.author: Sgt. Marcus Webb (Ret.)

articles.title: Choosing Your First Defensive Firearm: A Practical Guide
articles.excerpt: With thousands of handguns on the market, first-time buyers are overwhelmed. Here's the framework our instructors use when advising new students.
articles.body:
## The Wrong Way to Choose

Most people buy their first defensive firearm based on what a friend owns, what looked cool at the gun store, or what was on sale. None of these are good criteria.

## Our Selection Framework

1. **Ergonomic fit** — Can you reach the trigger with a proper grip?
2. **Reliability** — Has the model been proven reliable with a wide variety of ammunition?
3. **Caliber** — For defensive use, the 9mm offers the best balance of capacity, recoil, and terminal performance.
4. **Concealability** — Full-size pistols are easier to shoot accurately but harder to carry all day.
5. **Maintenance** — You should be able to field-strip, clean, and reassemble without a manual.
articles.author: Lt. Dana Hargrove (Ret.)
